quote: Take responsibility, feel the remorse, then rectify if you can, and then let it go.
change: Cut that sentence, the first of its paragraph. The very next sentence in the same paragraph already carries all of it at greater length: "Be specific about the action you took, and the impact it had, feel the remorse, do what you can to rectify or keep it from happening again, and then stop holding yourself hostage." (owning the action = "Be specific about the action you took"; "feel the remorse" is in both; "rectify if you can" = "do what you can to rectify"; "let it go" = "stop holding yourself hostage"). The paragraph then opens at "Be specific about the action you took,". No other words change.

keeps: The long sentence untouched, with its one addition ("or keep it from happening again") and its closing line about holding yourself hostage. heading: Forgiveness without bypass

section: A response check, not a verdict about what it is
quote: Internalize the fact that you don’t have to know where it comes from.
change: In the section's last paragraph, cut the first two sentences: "Internalize the fact that you don’t have to know where it comes from. Check in with yourself about whether or not this is helpful." Both are said earlier in the section: "Internalize the fact that you don’t have to know what it is." and "Find out if it helps to be warm towards it or to keep it at arm’s length" (paragraph 2), and "check in with yourself and see what’s best to do" (paragraph 1). heading: A response check, not a verdict about what it is

section: If it might be psychosis or destabilization
quote: The General Rule is: if you find that what you're doing is making you more loving, more grounded, more relational, more honest, more functional, then it's probably OK to keep doing it gently.
change: Put the heading "The General Rule" (his own term, from the paragraph's first words) before the section's last paragraph. "If it might be psychosis or destabilization" then keeps its first two paragraphs (the premise, then the list of signs ending "get help immediately. It’s not something to deal with in hypnosis."). keeps: The paragraph itself, unchanged and in its place straight after the list of signs it echoes, so the safeguard stays next to its step; both its permission half ("it's probably OK to keep doing it gently") and its "DON'T GO DEEPER! GET HELP!" ending.
heading: If it might be psychosis or destabilization
note: The rule is for the whole practice, not only for suspected psychosis; with the heading, the contents show it.

section: Appendix J: A practical induction library
quote: Once you start an induction, you will want to notice what’s going on (even if nothing changes) and work out what to do next, move, imagine something else, change the sensory channel you’re using, do nothing, stop the induction sequence and do something else… .
change: A paragraph break only, no label and no words changed: start a new paragraph at "Once you start an induction," and carry it to the end of the paragraph ("...at the end of an induction.").
